summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of renal transplant failure was admitted for fever and rigors following manipulation of his tunneled dialysis line. He was found to have MSSA bacteremia, and the infected line was exchanged over a guidewire. Blood and catheter tip cultures confirmed Staphylococcus aureus, and he was transitioned from vancomycin and gentamicin to cefazolin, which he will continue for four weeks. Repeat blood cultures remained negative, and a transthoracic echocardiogram showed no evidence of endocarditis. Tacrolimus was discontinued as it was no longer needed post-transplant failure. The patient improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home in stable condition with plans for ongoing antibiotic administration during dialysis and close monitoring for recurrence.
